name: Hustler Fund — Personal Loan
description: Instant mobile loan from the government via Safaricom. Borrow up to Ksh 50,000 at just 8% per year (0.002% per day). Repay in 14 days. 5% of every loan goes into a savings account in your name.
howToApply:
1. Dial *254# on Safaricom
2. Select 'Hustler Fund'
3. Choose 'Personal Finance'
4. Enter amount and confirm with M-Pesa PIN
documents: Safaricom SIM registered in your name (Huduma Namba or National ID used during SIM registration)

name: Youth Enterprise Development Fund (YEDF)
provider: Government of Kenya — State Department for Youth
description: Low-interest loans for young Kenyans to start or grow businesses. Interest rates from 0–8% per year. Can apply as an individual or as a group. Specifically supports youth in technology, agriculture, manufacturing, and services.
howToApply:
1. Register on yedf.go.ke
2. Fill in the online application form
3. Attach required documents
4. Visit your Sub-County Youth Development Office for verification
5. Wait for approval (typically 2–4 weeks)
documents: National ID, KRA PIN, Business registration certificate (if existing business), Business plan, Recent passport photo, Bank statement (3 months)

name: Uwezo Fund
description: Interest-free loans for registered groups of youth, women, and persons with disabilities. The government gives money at constituency level — your group applies through the local NG-CDF office.
howToApply:
1. Form or join a registered group (min 10 members)
2. Register the group with Department of Social Services
3. Visit your constituency NG-CDF office
4. Fill application form with group records
5. Group repays over 12–24 months
documents: Group registration certificate, Group minutes and constitution, Members' National IDs, Group bank account details, Group business plan
deadline: Rolling — check with your constituency NG-CDF office

name: Women Enterprise Fund (WEF)
description: Loans and capacity-building support specifically for women entrepreneurs. Apply individually or as a women's group. Funds disbursed through Equity Bank, KCB, and Co-op Bank. Also accessible via *254# on Safaricom.
amount: Up to Ksh 5,000,000 (group). Individual amounts vary.
howToApply:
1. Dial *254# on Safaricom OR visit wef.go.ke
2. Select Women Enterprise Fund
3. Apply individually or as a registered women's group
4. Funds disbursed through partner banks
documents: National ID, KRA PIN, Business registration (if applicable), Group registration certificate (for group applications), Passport photo

name: AGPO — Government Tenders (30% Reserved)
description: 30% of ALL government tenders are reserved for youth, women, and persons with disabilities by law. Once AGPO-certified, you can bid on government contracts worth millions — websites, printing, supplies, construction, services. Massively underused.
amount: Varies — tenders range from Ksh 50,000 to millions
howToApply:
1. Register your business (sole proprietor or company)
2. Get KRA PIN and tax compliance certificate
3. Apply for AGPO certificate at agpo.go.ke
4. Once certified, browse and bid on tenders at tenders.go.ke
documents: Business registration certificate, KRA PIN, National ID, Tax compliance certificate, Bank account in business name
deadline: Apply for AGPO certificate any time. Tenders are listed continuously.

name: KIEP 250+ Grant (World Bank)
provider: Kenya Industry & Entrepreneurship Project / World Bank
description: Ksh 7.5 billion World Bank programme providing performance-based grants, mentorship, and technical assistance to Kenyan SMEs. Cohort II is currently open. If you have a business that has been operating for at least 2 years, this is one of the largest grant opportunities available.
amount: Grant amount varies based on business needs and growth plan
howToApply:
1. Visit kiep.go.ke
2. Check eligibility (2+ years in operation)
3. Fill online application
4. Shortlisted businesses receive site visits and tailored support packages
documents: Business registration, KRA PIN, Audited accounts or financial statements (2 years), Business plan, National ID of directors
deadline: Cohort II — check kiep.go.ke for current deadline

name: WIDU Africa Grant
description: Grants of up to EUR 3,000 (first application) and EUR 5,000 (subsequent rounds) for Kenyan entrepreneurs. Especially relevant if you have relatives in EU countries, Switzerland, or Norway. Also runs #GreenKenya grants for eco-friendly businesses.
howToApply:
1. Visit widu.africa
2. Create an account
3. Submit business profile and growth plan
4. If you have a sponsor (EU-based relative), link their profile
documents: National ID, Business registration, Business plan, Bank account details, Sponsor details (if applicable)
deadline: Rolling — check widu.africa for active calls

name: Ward SME Grant (Ksh 50,000)
provider: Government of Kenya / World Bank — Ward Level
description: The government committed Ksh 5 billion for 100,000 small businesses — Ksh 50,000 per business across all 1,450 wards. This money is distributed at ward level. Most people don't know it exists. Visit your ward office and ask specifically about this fund.
amount: Ksh 50,000 (grant — does not need to be repaid)
howToApply:
1. Visit your Ward Administrator's office
2. Ask about the 'SME Ward Grant' or 'World Bank SME fund'
3. Fill application at the ward office
4. Provide required business documents
documents: National ID, Business registration OR evidence of business activity, KRA PIN, Passport photo
deadline: Ongoing — visit your ward office this week

name: SHA — Social Health Authority Cover
description: Kenya's new national health insurance replacing NHIF. Covers outpatient and inpatient services at government and accredited private hospitals. Every Kenyan should register. As of 2025, 4.5 million Kenyans have already received medical services worth Ksh 41 billion.
howToApply:
1. Dial *147# on any network OR visit sha.go.ke
2. Register yourself and dependants
3. Pay monthly contributions based on your income
4. Use SHA card at any accredited facility
documents: National ID or birth certificate, Huduma Namba (if available)

name: National Fund for the Disabled of Kenya (NFDK)
description: Financial grants, assistive devices, and support for persons with disabilities. Covers mobility aids, hearing aids, visual aids, and rehabilitation. Also funds disability-led businesses and organisations.
amount: Varies — assistive devices, rehabilitation funding, and business grants
howToApply:
1. Get a disability certificate from the National Council for Persons with Disabilities
2. Apply at nfdk.go.ke
3. Specify the type of support needed
documents: National ID, Disability assessment certificate (from NCPWD), Medical report from a registered doctor

name: Google Hustle Academy
description: Free AI-powered business training, mentorship, and access to Google's entrepreneurial network for Kenyan SMEs. No cost to apply. Gives you credibility, skills, and investor connections. Applications open for 2026 cohort.
howToApply:
1. Search 'Google Hustle Academy Kenya 2026' for current application link
2. Fill in the online application (takes ~20 minutes)
3. Describe your business and growth plans
documents: None required for initial application

name: National Youth Service (NYS) Recruitment
description: Government programme that provides skills training, employment, and stipends for young Kenyans. Covers construction, agriculture, ICT, healthcare, and more. Offers a pathway to government employment and entrepreneurship.
amount: Monthly stipend during training + skills certification
howToApply:
1. Check nys.go.ke for open recruitment periods
2. Apply online during recruitment windows
3. Attend physical selection at your county NYS office
documents: National ID, KCSE certificate, Birth certificate, Passport photos

name: LSK Legal Aid — Free Legal Representation
description: Free legal advice and representation for Kenyans who cannot afford a lawyer. Covers civil matters, family law, employment disputes, land cases, and more. Available through LSK offices in major towns.
howToApply:
1. Visit the LSK office in your county town
2. Explain your legal issue to the receptionist
3. You will be assessed for eligibility (based on income)
4. Assigned a pro bono lawyer if you qualify
documents: National ID, Any documents related to your legal issue

name: Judiciary Legal Aid Service
description: The Judiciary provides free legal aid at court stations for those who cannot afford representation. Available in high courts and magistrate courts across Kenya. Especially useful for criminal matters and family disputes.
howToApply:
1. Visit the nearest court station
2. Go to the Legal Aid desk
3. Explain your case and financial situation
4. Receive free representation if eligible
documents: National ID, Any court documents or charge sheets related to your case

name: Boma Yangu — Affordable Housing
description: Government affordable housing programme. Register to be allocated low-cost housing units across Kenya. Monthly contributions from Ksh 1,000. Units priced far below market rate for registered members.
howToApply:
1. Visit bomayangu.go.ke
2. Register with National ID and phone number
3. Choose preferred county and unit type
4. Make monthly contributions via M-Pesa
5. Wait for allocation balloting
documents: National ID, Active phone number, M-Pesa account

name: Inua Jamii Cash Transfer Programme
provider: Government of Kenya — Ministry of Labour & Social Protection
description: Monthly cash transfers for Kenya's most vulnerable: older persons aged 70+, orphans and vulnerable children (OVC), and persons with severe disabilities. Payments are made via M-Pesa every two months. Over 1.3 million households are enrolled nationwide.
amount: Ksh 2,000 – Ksh 4,000 per month (varies by category)
howToApply:
1. Visit your Sub-County Social Development Office
2. Ask for Inua Jamii registration
3. Fill the application form for your category (elderly, OVC, or disability)
4. Provide required documents for verification
5. If approved, payments start within 2–3 months via M-Pesa
documents: National ID or birth certificate, Huduma Namba, Disability assessment certificate (for PWD category), Death certificate of parent/guardian (for OVC), Proof of age (for elderly 70+)
deadline: Rolling — register at your Sub-County office

name: Hunger Safety Net Programme (HSNP)
provider: Government of Kenya / World Bank — NDMA
description: Cash transfer programme for the poorest households in Kenya's arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL). Covers Turkana, Marsabit, Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, Tana River, Isiolo, and Samburu counties. Payments every two months via M-Pesa to help families buy food and essentials.
howToApply:
1. HSNP uses a community targeting process — no walk-in applications
2. Community committees identify eligible households in your village
3. If selected, you receive an SMS and M-Pesa registration visit
4. Contact your county NDMA office to confirm if your household is enrolled
5. Visit ndma.go.ke for county office contacts
documents: National ID, Active Safaricom line for M-Pesa, Proof of residence in an HSNP county
deadline: Rolling — community targeting ongoing in ASAL counties

name: NG-CDF Bursary Scheme
description: Education bursaries funded through your MP's constituency office for secondary school, college, and university students from needy backgrounds. Each constituency allocates funds annually — amounts and deadlines vary by area. One of the most accessible education funds for ordinary Kenyans.
amount: Ksh 10,000 – Ksh 50,000 per year (varies by constituency)
howToApply:
1. Visit your constituency NG-CDF office (find it via ngcdf.go.ke)
2. Ask for the current bursary application form
3. Fill in student and guardian details
4. Attach required documents
5. Submit before the constituency deadline (usually Jan–Mar each year)
documents: National ID (student and parent/guardian), Admission letter or school fees structure, KCSE/KCPE results slip, Birth certificate, Recommendation letter from school principal
deadline: Annual — typically January to March (check your constituency office)

name: Kenya Youth Empowerment Project (KYEP)
description: Government programme providing skills training, internships, and stipends for unemployed youth. Covers sectors including construction, hospitality, ICT, and manufacturing. Combines classroom training with paid work placements at partner companies.
amount: Monthly stipend during training + job placement support
howToApply:
1. Check kyep.go.ke or Ministry of Youth website for open cohorts
2. Register online during recruitment windows
3. Select your preferred training sector
4. Attend orientation at your county youth office
5. Complete training and internship placement
documents: National ID, KCSE certificate, Birth certificate, Passport photos, Unemployment affidavit (if required)

name: Ajira Digital Programme
description: Free government programme training Kenyan youth for online digital jobs — data entry, transcription, virtual assistance, content writing, and software development. Access to Ajira Digital centres nationwide with free internet, mentorship, and links to global freelancing platforms.
amount: Free training + access to online job platforms (earn Ksh 15,000–Ksh 80,000/month)
howToApply:
1. Visit ajiradigital.go.ke
2. Register for an account
3. Enrol in a training track (data, transcription, dev, etc.)
4. Visit your nearest Ajira Digital centre for in-person support
5. Complete certification and start bidding on online jobs
documents: National ID, Active email address, KCSE certificate (for some tracks)

name: Kenya Women and Youth Enterprise Fund
provider: Government of Kenya — Ministry of Co-operatives & MSMEs
description: Merged fund combining the Women Enterprise Fund and Youth Enterprise Development Fund. Provides affordable loans and business support for women and youth entrepreneurs. Disbursed through partner banks including Equity, KCB, and Co-operative Bank.
amount: Up to Ksh 5,000,000 (terms vary by applicant profile)
howToApply:
1. Visit kwyef.go.ke or your nearest partner bank branch
2. Register and complete the online application
3. Attach business plan and required documents
4. Visit Sub-County office for verification
5. Loan disbursed through partner bank upon approval
documents: National ID, KRA PIN, Business registration certificate, Business plan, Bank statements (3 months), Passport photo

name: KCB 2Jiajiri Programme
description: KCB Foundation's flagship youth programme providing skills training, business incubation, and market linkages for young Kenyans. Covers agribusiness, automotive, beauty, construction, and ICT. Graduates receive certification and access to KCB micro-loans to start businesses.
amount: Free training + access to KCB Foundation loans (from Ksh 50,000)
howToApply:
1. Visit kcbgroup.com/2jiajiri or your nearest KCB branch
2. Check open training cohorts in your county
3. Apply online with personal and education details
4. Attend selection interview
5. Complete training and access loan facilities
documents: National ID, KCSE certificate, Birth certificate, Passport photos, Business proposal (for loan track)
deadline: Rolling — cohorts open throughout the year

name: County Youth & Women Enterprise Funds
provider: County Governments — Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru
description: County-level funds providing loans and grants for youth and women entrepreneurs. Nairobi Hasira Fund, Mombasa Biashara Fund, Kisumu Oyugis Youth Fund, and Nakuru County Empowerment Fund offer locally administered financing with easier access than national programmes. Visit your county trade or youth office.
howToApply:
Nairobi: Visit City Hall Trade department or nairobi.go.ke
Mombasa: Visit Mombasa County Trade office
Kisumu: Visit Kisumu County Youth and Sports office
Nakuru: Visit Nakuru County Trade and Industrialisation office
All: Fill county application form, attach business plan, await ward-level vetting
documents: National ID, KRA PIN, Business registration or business plan, Proof of county residence, Passport photo
deadline: Rolling — check with your county office

name: Equity Bank Fanikisha Loan
description: Micro-loans for small business owners and traders through Equity Bank. Available via Equitel, Equity mobile app, or branch. No collateral required for amounts under Ksh 100,000. One of the fastest ways to get business capital if you have an Equity Bank account.
howToApply:
1. Open an Equity Bank account (if you don't have one)
2. Dial *247# on Equitel OR use the Equity mobile app
3. Select 'Loans' then 'Fanikisha'
4. Enter amount and confirm
5. Funds disbursed instantly to your account
documents: National ID, Equity Bank account (6+ months active), KRA PIN (for larger amounts)

name: Safaricom Spark Venture Fund
description: Investment fund for early-stage Kenyan tech startups building on mobile, fintech, agritech, and healthtech. Provides funding plus access to Safaricom's 40+ million customer base, technical mentorship, and market distribution. Highly competitive but transformative for qualifying startups.
howToApply:
1. Visit spark.co.ke or safaricom.co.ke/spark
2. Review current investment themes and criteria
3. Submit pitch deck and business plan online
4. Shortlisted startups present to investment committee
5. Due diligence and term sheet negotiation
documents: Business registration, Pitch deck, Financial projections, Product demo or MVP, Founders' National IDs

name: Google for Startups Africa
description: Google's accelerator and funding programme for African startups. Provides equity-free support, Google Cloud credits (up to $100,000), mentorship from Google engineers, and access to investor networks. Kenya is a priority market with multiple Kenyan startups accepted each cohort.
amount: Up to $100,000 in Google Cloud credits + mentorship (equity-free)
howToApply:
1. Visit startup.google.com/programs/accelerator/africa
2. Check open application windows
3. Submit startup profile, traction metrics, and team details
4. Complete interview rounds if shortlisted
5. Join 3-month accelerator programme if selected
documents: Business registration, Pitch deck, Product URL or demo, Founders' LinkedIn profiles, Traction metrics
deadline: Cohort applications — check startup.google.com for dates

name: Developpp Ventures Grant
description: Impact investment fund backing Kenyan startups solving social and environmental challenges. Focus areas include agriculture, clean energy, financial inclusion, and healthcare. Provides grant funding and hands-on venture building support for early-stage founders.
howToApply:
1. Visit developpp.vc
2. Review current focus areas and portfolio
3. Submit application with impact thesis and business model
4. Pitch to investment team
5. Due diligence and grant disbursement
documents: Business registration, Impact measurement plan, Financial model, Founders' CVs, National IDs
deadline: Rolling — check developpp.vc for active calls

name: Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme
description: Africa's largest philanthropy-funded entrepreneurship programme. Provides USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital plus 12 weeks of business training and mentorship to 1,000 African entrepreneurs annually. Kenyan founders are consistently among the top recipients.
howToApply:
1. Visit tonyelumelufoundation.org during the annual application window (usually Jan–Mar)
2. Create an account and complete the business profile
3. Submit business idea and growth plan
4. Complete online training modules if shortlisted
5. Receive seed capital upon programme completion
documents: National ID, Business registration (or business plan for new ventures), Bank account details, Passport photo
deadline: Annual — typically January to March (check tonyelumelufoundation.org)

name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Programme
description: Full scholarships for academically talented Kenyan students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Covers tuition, accommodation, books, and stipends at partner universities including University of Nairobi, Strathmore, and USIU. Also supports secondary school bursaries through partner NGOs.
howToApply:
1. Visit mastercardfdn.org/scholars for partner institutions
2. Apply directly through the partner university during their intake period
3. Complete financial need assessment
4. Attend interview if shortlisted
5. Scholarship awarded before academic year starts
documents: KCSE results, National ID or birth certificate, Recommendation letters, Financial need statement, Admission letter (if available)
deadline: Varies by partner university — typically August to October

name: USAID Kenya Grants & Partnerships
description: US Government funding for Kenyan organisations working in health, agriculture, education, governance, and economic growth. Open to registered NGOs, social enterprises, and community-based organisations. Grants range from small community projects to multi-million dollar partnerships.
howToApply:
1. Register on grants.gov (for US entities) or usaid.gov/kenya for local opportunities
2. Monitor opportunity notices on usaid.gov/work-usaid/get-grant-or-contract
3. Submit concept note or full proposal as specified
4. Undergo technical and financial review
5. Sign grant agreement upon award
documents: Organisation registration certificate, KRA PIN, Audited financial statements, Project proposal and budget, Board resolution authorising application
deadline: Rolling — new opportunities posted throughout the year
